pk.context: 40 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is about 77%, and food does not alter the peak level or extent of absorption. About 98% is bound to protein, and about 71% of a dose is excreted in urine after hepatic metabolism.
clues.substance: A sodium salt in sesquihydrate form, with a molecular weight of 383.4 for the active moiety. It is a crystalline powder that is racemic and freely soluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 20 mg and 40 mg delayed-release tablets, plus a 40 mg packet of granules for oral suspension.
clues.safety: Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or its chemical relatives and with rilpivirine-containing products, with no boxed warning. Headache and diarrhea are the most frequent adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Short-term treatment and maintenance of healing in erosive esophagitis associated with reflux disease, and pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
clues.mechanism: Covalently binds the (H+,K+)-ATPase of gastric parietal cells, inhibiting both basal and stimulated acid secretion for more than 24 hours.

tell: An antisecretory effect lasting longer than 24 hours, despite a one-hour half-life, sets this proton pump inhibitor apart.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: the time to reach the peak concentration (t max ) is 2.5 h
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: with a terminal elimination half-life of approximately one hour
